articleTitle: Optimal placement of D-STATCOM and PV solar in distribution system using probabilistic load models
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: this paper proposes a hybrid analytical and metaheuristic optimization technique to find the proper locations and sizes for the distributed generator (DG) and Distribution Static Synchronous Compensator (D-STATCOM) in distribution networks to minimize the total losses and improve the voltage profile. The D-STATCOM and DGs are arranged in order to reduce line losses and improve the voltage profile of the system. For this goal, the important parameters of a bus are optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. probabilistic load model also is calculated using Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) method. Effectiveness of modified method is tested in a real distribution system of south Kerman (DSSK).

articleTitle: MPPT Control of a PMSG Connected to the Wind Turbine based on Deep Q-Network
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Due to the significant growth of artificial intelligence methods, especially deep reinforcement learning in solving uncertainty problems, using the Q-learning-based methods to control the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) of the wind turbine has more advantages than classic or non-intelligent methods. However, these methods also have disadvantages due to the discrete set of states and actions. This paper proposes a deep Q-network (DQN) approach for controlling the MPPT of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) connected to the wind turbine. This approach preserves the advantages of the Q-learning method and addresses the method’s pre-existing disadvantages as closely as possible. Unlike the Q-learning method, this algorithm has a set of contiguous states. The value function is approximated, and the optimal policy is obtained by utilizing a deep neural network. In each iteration of the learning process, the wind speed is varied randomly to train the intelligent agent, and the system is rewarded for its actions. The perturbation and observation approach is used for comparison of the described method. The approach harvests a greater proportion of the energy from the wind and demonstrates improved dynamic behaviour against wind speed variations.

articleTitle: Forecasting the PV Panel Power Based on Image Processing and Historical Outputs
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Solar PhotoVoltaic (PV) installment is expanding quickly around the world, but deeper integration into the electrical grid is hampered by solar power intermittency. A portion of the short-term PV fluctuation is caused by abrupt weather changes, such as cloud cover variations, which can drastically impact the PV panel output on time scales of minutes. Images of the sky can be used to provide information on the present and upcoming cloud cover to increase the accuracy of the PV power forecast. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used in this study so as to link the solar panels’ power with the current sky photos. In addition, the PV panel’s historical output is utilized to enhance forecasting accuracy. Also, the sensitivity of the proposed model to the configuration of the machine learning procedure, such as the number of neurons and the width of the network, has been assessed. Furthermore, the uncertainty of the incorporated stochastic approach and the effect of different arrangements of inputs and outputs on the performance metrics have been evaluated. The proposed model achieves the root mean square error ranges from 2.37 kW to 3.43 kW for the real-data dataset.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Microgrid in the Presence of Distributed Energy Resources and Demand Response Programs
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and operation planning of microgrid. The multi-objective optimization of microgrid operation is done in the form of eight scenarios in the presence of renewable energies, diesel generators, battery energy storage system, and demand response (DR) programs. The DR programs used in this paper include various incentive-based and time-based programs with the power model, which is the most non-conservative nonlinear DR model. The Monte Carlo simulation is used to predict solar irradiance and wind speed. At the end of the study, the results of simulation scenarios are compared with each other, the effects of DR programs on microgrid operation are discussed and the best DR program is chosen.

articleTitle: Estimation of Solar Cell Circuit Model Parameters Using an Algorithm Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this article, it is intended to estimate the parameters of the equivalent circuit of the two-diode model of the PV system by using the method based on artificial intelligence. Based on this, at first, using the particle swarm algorithm as a suitable method, 7 parameters of the two-diode model were optimized. In order to check the performance of the particle swarm method, different strategies were considered for it, including PSO algorithm with random inertia coefficient, time-varying inertia coefficient, time-varying learning coefficients, contraction coefficient and average. Next, the Archimedes optimization method as a new algorithm in this field was proposed and investigated, and the parameters of the two-diode model were optimized based on it. In order to check the accuracy of the proposed methods, the results obtained from the optimization of the parameters of the two-diode PV system model were compared with some optimization methods.

articleTitle: A Fast Fault Detection Method for Protection of HVDC Transmission using Voltage of The PMFCL
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems efficiently carry significant amounts of renewable energy. An smoothing reactor (SR) has a poor ability to decrease the short-circuit current in the HVDC transmission line. The SR can be replaced by a permanent magnet-type saturated-core fault current limiter (PMFCL). The PMFCL behaves like the SR when operating normally for power quality reasons. Its inductance immediately rises in a short-circuit state and reduces the fault current. Detecting a high-resistance fault using the PMFCL is easier than that of the SR, which is caused by an increase in the inductance value. This paper proposes a fast fault detection method for the protection of the HVDC transmission lines using the voltage across the PMFCL. The proposed method can detect high-resistance faults in approximately 1 millisecond. The method does not cause the DC circuit breaker (DCCB) to malfunction during load changes and AC faults and is safe from noise. The PMFCL reduces the strict requirements on the protection scheme and DCCB, improving the grid’s operational safety.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Simulation of a Rooftop Photovolataic System in Faculty of Engineering Guilan University
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, simulation and study the rooftop photovoltaic system on building roofs of the faculty of engineering Guilan university, Iran. It is now clear that conventional plants heavily contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, so they are not environmentally friendly. Renewable energy sources are an alternative solution. In this study, the design of a grid-connected photovoltaic system was simulated. PV panels and the number of inverters are the main elements of the PV power system. According to the regional weather data and university ceiling structure, shadow analysis, calculation concerning the total number of panels, number of strings, and number of panels per string, and their optimal angles are done. PVSYST software is used for the proposed photovoltaic system design

articleTitle: Fault detection and reconfiguration of the 12-pulse thyristor rectifier
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Providing power through a silicon-controlled rectifier (SCR) is still commercially efficient. This type of rectifier is a well-known choice for converters in the high power range. Especially new exciter with SCR exciter is proliferating in generators. Monitoring, supervision, and safety checking of this kind of converter could increase reliability and decrease the risk of losses and penalties for interrupting the power supply of susceptible systems. In this paper, a fast, simple, robust fault detection and identification system with a small number of calculations have been proposed to detect open circuit fault of three-phase SCR (6-pulse, 12-pulse…). In addition, a strategy to reconfigure a 12-pulse converter is proposed. The simulation in MATLAB/SIMULINK has shown the acceptable performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Effect of light spectrum on the performance of SMFC with microalgae improved cathode
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Sediment microbial fuel cells as a renewable energy production system can directly convert chemical energy into electricity. In these cells, the microorganisms present in the anode oxidize organic materials in anaerobic conditions and produce electrons. The generated electrons move to the cathode electrode via an external circuit and reduce the electron acceptor present in the cathode section. In this study, the microalgae Chlorella sp. has been used in cathode to produce oxygen, as terminal electron acceptor, during the photosynthesis process. In this study, the effect of three light colors (white, blue or red) at constant intensity (47.33±2.39 μmolphoton m-2s-1) was studied. The results showed that the photosynthetic sediment microbial fuel cells (PSMFCs) under red, white, and blue colors produced a maximum pseudo-steady voltage of 99.31±1.48 mV,110.17±1.33 mV, and 95.2±2.85 mV, respectively. Also, maximum power densities of 4.39 mW/m2, 3.57 mW/m2, and 1.5 mW/m2 were obtained. The findings showed that the PSMFC under red color had better performance in terms of electricity generation.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Internet of Things Technology in the Smart Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Pollution and climate change are two outcomes of the ever-increasing energy consumption that has accompanied the rise in urbanization and the overall human population; moreover, the current power grid cannot keep up with the rising electrical demand of recent decades. Relying on renewable energy sources is often cited as a way to address these issues as of late. Yet, the limitations of the existing power infrastructure render it impossible to implement solutions such as increasing the use of RE sources and optimizing energy consumption. A multitude of problems can be tackled by implementing the smart grids (SGs), but there are obstacles to their widespread adoption, such as security concerns, that can be addressed by employing cutting-edge technology like the Internet of Things (IoT). By increasing the effectiveness of energy systems and the utilization of renewable energy sources, IoT can be utilized to reduce the environmental impacts of energy consumption. From local to wide-area networks, IoT-enabled smart networks can improve performance in a variety of ways, including security, resource conservation, and cost savings. This paper will discuss the requirements for enabling the Internet of Things in SGs, the applications of IoT in SGs, standardization and protocols for implementation, and its challenges will be reviewed further.

articleTitle: Economic Evaluation of Supplying a Hotel by DGs in the condition of Khuzestan Province Using Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of various variables on consumption of a typical hotel in the conditions of Khuzestan province is studied. These variables are diesel fuel price and its limitation, expected inflation rate, nominal discount rate, carbon dioxide (CO<inf>2</inf>) emission penalty, and annual capacity shortage. Also, the effect of temperature on photovoltaic panels (PVs) is considered. Cases are studied using HOMER software and the impact of each of the mentioned variables on economic parameters like net present cost (NPC) and cost of energy (COE), is presented. It is observed that with the increase in fuel prices, consideration of restrictions on fuel supply and presence of penalty for the emission of CO<inf>2</inf>, the use of renewable sources is economic. Also, with the rise in percentage of annual capacity shortage and fall in inflation rate and the discount rate, the total cost of the project decreases.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization for Simultaneous Optimal Sizing & Placement of DGs and D-STATCOM in Distribution Networks Using Artificial Rabbits Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: It is becoming more important to use electric networks efficiently as power grids expand and modernize. Reducing existing challenges, such as excessive power losses, poor voltage profiles, voltage instability, unreliable operation, etc., is essential due to the high cost of constructing and expanding power grids. Today, minimizing losses in network distribution is crucial. On the other hand, distribution networks are using distributed generation sources (DGs) much more commonly. o prevent these problems, Distribution Synchronous Static Compensator (D-STACTOM) can be used in electric distribution networks as a shunt compensator device. Economic feasibility, needed quality, dependability, and availability should all be considered while deciding on the best location and size for D-STACOM. Therefore, by picking the appropriate place and size, these resources can play a crucial part in lowering the power losses of distribution networks. D-FACTS tools like D-STATCOM in distribution networks and DGs can significantly contribute to reducing losses and compensating reactive power. The optimal sizing & placement of DGs and D-STATCOM in the radial distribution network is covered in this article. The proposed method’s desired outcomes include lowering active power losses, enhancing voltage stability and profile, and minimizing costs. The Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) algorithm has resolved this optimization issue. The IEEE 33 bus standard system tests the suggested method for analysis. The results are compared with two algorithms, Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) and Emperor Penguins Colony (EPS), to investigate the capability of the algorithm proposed for optimal sizing and placement problems. According to the simulation results, the ideal placement and size for DGs and D-STATCOM can significantly lower network losses and enhance the voltage profile.

articleTitle: Optimal Low-Power SI-MIMO Converter for Renewable Energy Base Power Supply of Wireless Gas Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In order to carry out efficient flammable gas leaks and emissions monitoring of pipelines, wireless sensor nodes have to be deployed at different locations and heights. Therefore, the power grid could be unavailable and the power supply of gas sensors should be based on battery-renewable energy which needs an optimal low-power switching algorithm considering low cost. In addition, it is important to save battery life by protecting the battery from full discharge and overcharging. This paper introduces a DC/DC single-inductor, multi-input, multi-output (SI-MIMO) converter that can operate in three modes: buck, buck-boost, and boost. This converter is going to be designed in the discrete form. The basis is that the CPU of the microcontroller be turned on as little as possible and to be used only when it is necessary. Digital algorithms are considered in such a way that the system can intelligently and, depending on the energy level of the inputs, can use them to charge the outputs and determine the optimal switching frequency for each output. The system can work with variable input. Each output can be charged at different frequencies and according to their load, and the maximum switching frequency is equal to 10 kHz, which is a relatively low frequency.

articleTitle: Investigating the Optimal Location Determination Index of Charging Stations from the Perspectives of Distribution Companies, Owners of Charging Stations and Owners of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Advances in technology and the expansion of the use of electric hybrid vehicles have created a new opportunity for the transportation system to prevent the increase in fossil fuel consumption and pollution in cities around the world. The development of charging stations in different areas and with different capacities is one of the most important issues for expanding the use of electric vehicles. Choosing the optimal location for charging stations for electric vehicles is an important issue that has been considered in recent years. Due to the effect of charging stations on the parameters of distribution networks, the appropriate location for the charging station from the perspective of energy supply companies may not be the same as the appropriate location of the charging station from the perspective of owners of electric vehicles. Appropriate locating indicators will vary from the point of view of electricity distribution companies, owners of electric vehicles, investors and owners of charging stations. Therefore, it is necessary to examine these indicators from different perspectives and finally to introduce the appropriate and optimal indicators. In this article, we have tried to introduce the improved locating of charging stations from the perspective of distribution companies, owners of electric vehicles and investors or owners of charging stations.

articleTitle: A Novel Game Theory-based Participation Model of a Microgrid in a Competitive Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2023 10th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, the ever-increasing electricity demand throughout the world along with the deficiencies related to large electric power systems have motivated researchers to take more attentions to practically efficient power generation alternatives such as distributed generations (DGs) based on renewable energies. This research investigates the operation of a microgrid with the aim of overall profit maximization for different players/participants in a competitive electricity market environment using game theory. The proposed microgrid consists of three main sections of generation, storage, and consumption with microturbines, wind turbines, batteries, electric vehicles, and residential loads. There is an electricity market pool for evaluation of market participants’ behavior and actions. The microgrid is able to buy/sell power from/to the upstream distribution network in different times within a 24-hr time horizon. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to optimize the final objective function considering different operational constraints in the problem.
